5º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 7

Healthy habits: should and shouldn't

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Give advice with should and shouldn't (dar consejos)
  • Learn vocabulary about health, food, sleep and exercise
  • Talk about common illnesses and what to do
  • Ask for advice: What should I do?

Para pensar

Tu amigo te dice que le duele la cabeza porque ha estado tres horas con la consola. ¿Qué consejo le darías en inglés?

Explicación

Healthy and unhealthy habits

A habit is something we do regularly. Healthy habits are good for our body and mind: eating fruit and vegetables, drinking water, sleeping well, doing exercise, washing our hands, brushing our teeth, spending time outdoors.

Unhealthy habits are bad for us: eating lots of sweets and fast food, drinking fizzy drinks, staying up late, sitting in front of a screen all day. En castellano: healthy es «sano» o «saludable», y unhealthy, lo contrario. El prefijo un- cambia el significado al opuesto.

Should for advice

We use should to give advice (consejos) or to say what is a good idea. The form is very easy: subject + should + verb (without to). «You should eat more vegetables.» «She should go to bed early.» «We should drink water when we play sports.»

Should is the same for all persons: I should, he should, they should. We never add -s («he shoulds») and we never use to after it («you should to eat»). En castellano: equivale a «deberías» o «sería bueno que».

Shouldn't: it's not a good idea

For the negative we use shouldn't (should not): «You shouldn't eat so many sweets.» «Children shouldn't sleep with the phone next to the bed.» «We shouldn't skip breakfast.»

We use it to say something is not a good idea. It is softer than an order. Compare: «Don't eat that!» (orden) and «You shouldn't eat that» (consejo). Pronunciación: should se dice «shud» (la l no suena) y shouldn't, «shúdnt».

What's the matter?

When someone looks ill, we ask What's the matter? (¿Qué te pasa?). They answer with I've got a… + problem: a headache (dolor de cabeza), a stomachache (de barriga), a toothache (de muelas), an earache (de oído), a sore throat (dolor de garganta), a cold (un resfriado), a cough (tos), a temperature (fiebre).

We can also say «I feel sick» (tengo náuseas) or «I'm tired». Truco: -ache significa «dolor» y se pronuncia «eik»: head-ache, stomach-ache.

Giving advice for illnesses

Now we can join both: the problem and the advice. «I've got a cold.» «You should stay in bed and drink hot milk with honey.» «I've got a toothache.» «You should go to the dentist. You shouldn't eat sweets.» «I've got a sore throat.» «You shouldn't shout or drink very cold drinks.»

If the problem is serious, the best advice is always: «You should see a doctor» or «You should tell an adult». Medicines are only for when a doctor or your family says so.

Asking for advice

To ask for advice we make a question: Should I…? or What should I do? «I'm always tired in class. What should I do?» «You should go to bed earlier.» «Should I take a jacket?» «Yes, you should. It's cold.» «No, you shouldn't.»

Other useful questions: «Do you think I should…?», «What do you think?». We can answer giving our opinion: «I think you should…», «I don't think you should…». These phrases make your advice sound kind and polite.

A balanced diet

To be healthy we should eat a balanced diet: a bit of everything, in the right amount. We should eat fruit and vegetables every day (five portions!), cereals and bread for energy, fish, eggs, beans and meat for protein, and milk and yoghurt for strong bones.

We shouldn't eat too much sugar, salt or fried food. And remember: water is the best drink. Use the plate: half vegetables and fruit, a quarter cereals, a quarter protein.

Reading: Doctor Sara answers

Read this letter to a children's magazine: «Dear Doctor Sara, I'm eleven and I'm always tired. I go to bed at midnight because I watch videos on my tablet. I don't have breakfast because I'm not hungry. What should I do? — Marcos.»

«Dear Marcos, you should sleep at least nine hours, so you should go to bed at ten. You shouldn't use your tablet in bed: the light keeps your brain awake. You should have a small breakfast, like fruit and yoghurt. And you should play outside every day. Good luck! — Doctor Sara.»

Let's practise: advice cards

In pairs, write problem cards: «I can't sleep», «I've got a stomachache», «I'm always hungry at break», «My eyes hurt after the computer». Mix the cards. Take one and read it; your partner gives two pieces of advice, one with should and one with shouldn't.

Then make a class poster: «10 healthy habits for 5th grade». Start each line with We should or We shouldn't. Repaso: should + verbo sin to; nunca «shoulds»; pregunta con «Should I…?» o «What should I do?».

Should and shouldn't

Ejercicios

  1. Complete: «You ___ brush your teeth after meals.»

  2. Complete: «You ___ watch TV all afternoon.»

  3. Translate: «dolor de garganta».

  4. Answer: «What's the matter?» (te duele la barriga)

  5. Give advice for: «I've got a temperature.»

  6. Correct: «She should to sleep more.»

  7. Make a question: «I / take / a jacket»

  8. Healthy or unhealthy? «drink fizzy drinks every day»

  9. Write two pieces of advice about screens.

  10. Write three healthy habits for your class poster.

Practica

  1. «Should» means…

    1. A) puedo
    2. B) tengo que
    3. C) debería

  2. «You ___ drink more water.»

    1. A) should
    2. B) should to
    3. C) shoulds

  3. «He ___ eat so much sugar.»

    1. A) don't should
    2. B) shouldn't
    3. C) shouldn't to

  4. «What's the matter?» means…

    1. A) ¿Qué hora es?
    2. B) ¿Qué te pasa?
    3. C) ¿Qué haces?

  5. «I've got a ___.» (dolor de cabeza)

    1. A) headpain
    2. B) head ache pain
    3. C) headache

  6. Which is a healthy habit?

    1. A) sleeping 10 hours
    2. B) skipping breakfast
    3. C) staying up late

  7. «___ I go to the doctor?»

    1. A) Do should
    2. B) Am should
    3. C) Should

  8. «a sore throat» is…

    1. A) tos
    2. B) dolor de garganta
    3. C) fiebre

  9. The best drink is…

    1. A) water
    2. B) cola
    3. C) energy drinks

  10. «Should» sounds like…

    1. A) «shud»
    2. B) «shuld»
    3. C) «sholed»

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve should y cómo se forma; Cómo se hace la negativa y la pregunta; Cómo se dice que te duele algo en inglés; Qué hábitos son sanos y cuáles no.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

shouldDeberías (consejo).
shouldn'tNo deberías.
What should I do?¿Qué debería hacer?
What's the matter?¿Qué te pasa?
headacheDolor de cabeza.
sore throatDolor de garganta.
healthy / unhealthySano / poco sano.
balanced dietDieta equilibrada.

Soluciones

  1. C) Sirve para aconsejar.
  2. A) Should + verbo.
  3. B) Negativa: shouldn't.
  4. B) Para preguntar por un problema.
  5. C) head + ache.
  6. A) Dormir bien.
  7. C) Pregunta: Should I…?
  8. B) Sore = dolorido.
  9. A) Agua.
  10. A) La l no suena.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. should.
  2. shouldn't.
  3. a sore throat.
  4. I've got a stomachache.
  5. You should stay in bed and see a doctor.
  6. She should sleep more.
  7. Should I take a jacket?
  8. Unhealthy: you shouldn't drink fizzy drinks every day.
  9. Model answer: You shouldn't use screens before bed. You should take breaks.
  10. Model answer: We should eat fruit at break. We should wash our hands. We shouldn't shout in class.
